purpose: Separate gas-phase oxygen/nitrogen physics from assimilable-nitrogen metabolism before attributing bacterial-cellulose changes to an O2+N2 state vector.

evidence_anchors.finding: Komagataeibacter cellulose production is strongly oxygen-dependent; low or controlled oxygen states can alter BC yield and material properties depending on strain and cultivation mode.
Dissolved oxygen controlled near 10% saturation maximized cellulose yield in one agitated fed-batch Acetobacter xylinum BRC5 system.
High carbon-dioxide partial pressure reduced BC production in agitated Acetobacter culture, creating a gas-composition confound distinct from oxygen.
Nitrogen-source identity significantly affected cellulose production across Komagataeibacter isolates; peptone outperformed ammonium sulfate and urea on average in the reported screen.
A 2026 K. xylinus study confirmed that nitrogen-normalized medium composition can materially change BC yield and structural characteristics.
One K. hansenii JR-02 isolate produced some BC in nitrogen-free medium and carried a possible nifH sequence; this is treated as strain-specific and not a genus-wide N2-fixation claim.

decision_rules.if: BC tracks dissolved O2/transfer state across gas mixtures while N2 fraction adds no reproducible residual after pO2, pCO2 and nutrient-N matching
BC changes with assimilable-N source or C:N while gas mediator vector is matched
N2-associated BC difference disappears after pO2/dissolved-O2 and pCO2 matching
A reproducible N2-associated residual survives pO2, dissolved-O2, pCO2, total-pressure, transfer, pH, osmolality and nutrient-N matching

Direct strain-specific nitrogen-fixation capability is independently verified and gas-phase N2 availability causally changes nitrogen incorporation or BC phenotype under matched gas-transfer conditions

kill_rules: If pCO2 is not measured or bounded, an O2:N2 gas-composition effect cannot be assigned to N2.
If dissolved oxygen or transfer state differs, gas-fraction comparisons cannot establish N2 specificity.
If assimilable nitrogen differs, gas N2 and nutrient-N interpretations must remain separate.
A possible nifH sequence in one isolate is not proof that the tested strain fixes N2.
A nanobubble result does not by itself distinguish gas chemistry from bubble-mediated mass transfer.
No universal O2+N2 law may be promoted from one strain or one cultivation geometry.
safety_boundary: This artifact is a non-operational research design. Compressed-gas, pressure-vessel, sterile-culture and laboratory handling require appropriate trained personnel, equipment and institutional procedures.
